about: The operating words of the system: one word, one meaning. This is how work is organised, for any brand. Where a meaning was already written down it is taken as written, not rewritten; 'source' says where. It does not define the creative words (angle, concept, framework, format, hook): those have their own home, named under 'elsewhere'. A use listed under 'retire' is renamed in the place that owns it, on the owner's yes, never here.

connect.rule: Nothing joins the system without one row in components.json. The row is the connection.
a_row_says: kind: tool, engine, library or definitions
does: what it does, in a few words
role: the role that owns it
workflow: which workflow, every workflow, or the system itself
steps: the steps inside it, if it has named ones
the_check_fails_when: a row names a role, workflow, stage or kind that does not exist
a listed tool is missing from the list
a word is given two meanings

two_copies.what: The same components live in two places: a team workspace and this toolkit.
two_copies.note: Not one shared component is the same file for file. Part of that is the toolkit's name-stripping; the two causes were not separated. No written rule was found for which copy leads. Even the approved stage list differs between the two copies. Decided 2026-11-17: the toolkit leads.

bridge.rule: The working copy follows the toolkit. A component is built or changed here first, then taken across. Nothing here reads or writes the working copy.
bridge.today: Changes have been flowing the other way: made in the working copy, then mirrored here with names stripped. Turning that around is the bridge's job.
